book_title: Prologue: The Vehicle, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What is MSTX, why has it lost 90.60% in 12 months, and what is our exact decision for new capital, current holdings, and capital redeployment?

epigraph.quote: Before you ask how much money a trade can make when you are right, ask what the math does to your capital while you wait.
epigraph.author: Institutional Risk & Portfolio Desk

web_blocks.html: Defiance Daily Target 2X Long MSTR ETF (NASDAQ: MSTX) is a single-stock leveraged ETF issued by Tidal Trust II and advised by Tidal Investments LLC [1, 2]. Its sole mandate is to deliver 200% of the daily return of Strategy Inc. (MSTR) before fees [1]. The fund uses total return swaps across four dealers: BMO Capital Markets, Clear Street, Cantor Fitzgerald, and Marex Capital Markets [2]. Segregated cash and U.S. Treasury bills back those swaps [2]. MSTX is not an operating business, holds no Bitcoin directly, and targets single-day traders only [1, 4].

Our two-pass underwriting assigns an unambiguous REJECTED verdict for new capital. Pass 1 stamped FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL and kpi_health: FAIL on the wrapper's economics [1, 2]. Pass 2 confirmed a Weinstein STAGE_4 downtrend at $8.75 on November 13, 2026, down -90.60% over 12 months after a 1-for-10 reverse split on March 19, 2026 [1, 3, 21]. On our current-holding ledger, Robinhood holds 148.481 shares ($1,299.21 market value, $1,663.83 cost basis, -$364.62 unrealized loss, 1.46% portfolio weight). Our holding action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 148.481 shares, redeploying 100% of the $1,299.21 proceeds to Cash / T-bills while the US market remains in a Correction [20].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to this institutional dossier on the Defiance Daily Target 2X Long MSTR ETF, ticker MSTX. Before you and I examine a single chart or SEC table, let's get crystal clear on what we are actually looking at. MSTX is not an operating company. It employs no engineers, sells no enterprise software, and mines no Bitcoin. Instead, it is a specialized exchange-traded wrapper inside Tidal Trust II whose sole daily mission is to deliver 200% of the single-day percentage return of Strategy Inc. (MSTR) before fees and expenses.

Why does a single-day leveraged ETF deserve a full ten-chapter forensic monograph? Because retail and tactical investors routinely confuse a low nominal share price—$8.75 as of Friday, November 13, 2026—with a 'cheap' long-term investment. In reality, that $8.75 quote exists only because MSTX executed a 1-for-10 reverse stock split on March 19, 2026 after losing more than 90% of its split-adjusted value from its $83.10 52-week high. When you stack 2x daily-resetting total-return swaps on top of a company whose own balance sheet is a leveraged Bitcoin treasury, the resulting volatility doesn't just rattle your nerves—it mathematically consumes your principal.

To keep our judgment completely free of price anchoring, we ran this underwriting in two strictly separated passes. In Pass 1, completely blind to the $8.75 stock price and technical chart, we audited MSTX's SEC Form 497K prospectus, Form N-CSRS semi-annual shareholder report, swap counterparty schedules, and cash-flow waterfall. That price-blind audit stamped MSTX with a FUNDAMENTAL FAIL rating and FAIL KPI health: its 1.31% unitary expense ratio, OBFR-plus-10%-to-17% embedded swap financing spreads, -$5.88 million six-month net investment loss, and forced taxable distributions of realized swap gains make it structurally unfit for multi-week or multi-year compounding.

In Pass 2, we unlocked the live November 13, 2026 market ledger and tested that fundamental reality against the tape. At $8.75, MSTX sits in a deep Stan Weinstein Stage 4 downtrend—44.79% below its 50-day moving average ($15.85), 48.71% below its 30-week moving average ($17.06), and 54.21% below its 200-day moving average ($19.11)—while the broader US equity market itself is in a Correction with six distribution days. Across our probability-weighted 12-month scenarios (20% Bull at $15.85, 50% Base decay at $5.50, 30% Bear at $2.50), MSTX carries an expected value of $6.67, or a -23.8% expected loss.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Our job as disciplined analysts is not to find an excuse to buy every ticker on a watchlist. Sometimes the highest-alpha decision in the entire book is a clear, unhedged REJECTED.

book_subsections.title: Our Dual Verdict & Capital Redeployment Plan
paragraphs: For new capital, MSTX is REJECTED across medium-term and long-term horizons, and we stand aside on short-term tactical trades. For current holdings, our positions ledger confirms 148.481 shares held in Robinhood ($1,299.21 market value at $8.75, $1,663.83 cost basis, -$364.62 unrealized loss, 1.46% portfolio weight). Our holding action is EXIT IMMEDIATELY across all 148.481 shares, redeploying 100% of the $1,299.21 proceeds into Treasury-bill cash (~3.9%–4.5% yield) while keeping Microsoft (MSFT) on our active shortlist watch and spot Bitcoin ETF IBIT (0.25% expense ratio) as our preferred unleveraged outside benchmark once Stage 2 uptrends return.

In the nine chapters that follow, you and I will trace MSTX from its explosive August 2024 debut and $1.67 billion asset peak through its four swap counterparties, $100 economic waterfall, competitive landscape against MSTU and IBIT, technical Stage 4 breakdown, and final action plan. Every number is reconciled directly to SEC filings and our November 13, 2026 market snapshot so you can judge the structure with total clarity.

book_subsections.title: What You Will Learn Across These Ten Chapters
paragraphs: Most commentary on single-stock leveraged ETFs stops at a surface-level warning about daily compounding. That is not enough for serious capital allocation. In Chapter 1, we trace MSTX from its August 14–15, 2024 launch at 1.75x leverage through its October 29, 2024 upgrade to 2.0x, its November 12, 2024 sprint past $1 billion in assets, its $1.67 billion peak in April 2025, and its subsequent 90% contraction and March 19, 2026 1-for-10 reverse split. In Chapters 2 and 3, we open the hood on Tidal Trust II's four swap counterparties—BMO Capital Markets, Clear Street, Cantor Fitzgerald, and Marex Capital Markets—and trace every dollar of fee, T-bill collateral yield, and OBFR-plus-10%-to-17% financing spread in a period-matched $100 waterfall.

In Chapters 4 through 6, we test MSTX against its direct competitor MSTU (which charges 1.05% versus MSTX's 1.31% on more than double the AUM), audit management's stated mandate against 4,006% annual portfolio turnover, and examine the $1.755 billion of paid-in capital versus -$1.173 billion in accumulated losses on the October 31, 2025 balance sheet. Finally, in Chapters 7 through 9, we bring that price-blind forensic record into the live November 13, 2026 market tape at $8.75, compare MSTX against MSTR, IBIT, and BITX, check the Stage 4 technical structure and 154.9% implied volatility options chain, and lock in our REJECTED verdict and 100% cash redeployment plan.
